This section is the **agent knowledge base**: short, scannable notes
about non-obvious things in this codebase that previous agents wished
they'd known earlier.

Each insight answers three questions in three short sections:

1. **What** — the fact, in one paragraph.
2. **Why it matters** — the failure mode it prevents, with a citation
   to the incident or commit that revealed it.
3. **How to apply** — what an agent should *do differently* given
   this knowledge.

## Reading

- **At session start**, run `docs:outline` and skim this section. The
  whole collection should take under a minute. Most "weird bugs" have
  an insight written.
- **When investigating a confusing failure**, `docs:search` for the
  symptom before grepping code.

## Contributing

See [authoring docs (PG-canonical)](/internal/docs/agent-insights/authoring-docs-pg-canonical)
for the authoring mechanics. Short version:

- Write one when you discover a non-obvious fact (PG quirk, library
  gotcha, subtle invariant, hidden cross-cutting rule).
- Don't write one when the fix lives in code, or when the thing is
  already documented elsewhere — update the existing doc instead.
- Keep it short — three sections, under 50 lines total.

If something is obsolete, set `status: superseded` or `retired` in
the frontmatter (don't delete the file) and add an "Update:/Superseded:"
note in the body. Entries stay in the sidebar and the generated
[insights index](/internal/docs/reference/agent-insights-index) regardless
of status — the index surfaces `status` as a column rather than hiding
non-active pages.
